items.title: John "Knocky" Parker Interview, 1963-08-28
items.q: Yes, lots of records with Bob Wills. He fit in ideally.

ctx.x: That's all I know. Tell them who he was. He was a trumpet player from Oklahoma, wasn't he originally? Or, I don't know. Maybe he was here. I thought he was here. No, I don't think so. Did he ever play in New Orleans? He may have. I don't know. I read something about him, and my memory is not as good as yours, and Dick Allen's. And all I know is he went out and he played with, I think he did some subbing with Lil Waters, and Turk, and all that gang. But he was maybe making a living. No, he was playing with Bob…
Yes, lots of records with Bob Wills. He fit in ideally. Yeah. That's the theory at any rate I was talking about. A good musician can do anything, and that's it.
Well, the music's worse. I mean, a good classical musician maybe or maybe couldn't fit into some of these other forms, but you felt the forms were close enough then.
